IMPORTANT: When the user asks you to create a pull request, follow these steps carefully:

1. Run the following bash commands in parallel using the Bash tool, in order to understand the current state of the branch since it diverged from the main branch:
   - Run a git status command to see all untracked files (never use -uall flag)
   - Run a git diff command to see both staged and unstaged changes that will be committed
   - Check if the current branch tracks a remote branch and is up to date with the remote, so you know if you need to push to the remote
   - Run a git log command and `git diff [base-branch]...HEAD` to understand the full commit history for the current branch (from the time it diverged from the base branch)
2. Analyze all changes that will be included in the pull request, making sure to look at all relevant commits (NOT just the latest commit, but ALL commits that will be included in the pull request!!!), and draft a pull request title and summary:
   - Keep the PR title short (under 70 characters)
   - Use the description/body for details, not the title
3. Run the following commands in parallel:
   - Create new branch if needed
   - Push to remote with -u flag if needed
   - Create PR using gh pr create with the format below. Use a HEREDOC to pass the body to ensure correct formatting. End the body with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.
<example>
gh pr create --title "the pr title" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary
<1-3 bullet points>

## Test plan
[Bulleted markdown checklist of TODOs for testing the pull request...]
EOF
)"
</example>

Important:
- DO NOT use the TaskCreate or Agent tools
- Return the PR URL when you're done, so the user can see it

# Other common operations
- View comments on a Github PR: gh api repos/foo/bar/pulls/123/comments

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem. You can access any file directly by using this tool.
Assume this tool is able to read all files on the machine. If the User provides a path to a file assume that path is valid. It is okay to read a file that does not exist; an error will be returned.

Usage:
- The file_path parameter must be an absolute path, not a relative path
- By default, it reads up to 2000 lines starting from the beginning of the file
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- This tool allows Claude Code to read images (eg PNG, JPG, etc). When reading an image file the contents are presented visually as Claude Code is a multimodal LLM.
- This tool can read PDF files (.pdf). For large PDFs (more than 10 pages), you MUST provide the pages parameter to read specific page ranges (e.g., pages: "1-5"). Reading a large PDF without the pages parameter will fail. Maximum 20 pages per request.
- This tool can read Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb files) and returns all cells with their outputs, combining code, text, and visualizations.
- This tool can only read files, not directories. To list files in a directory, use the registered shell tool.
- You will regularly be asked to read screenshots. If the user provides a path to a screenshot, ALWAYS use this tool to view the file at the path. This tool will work with all temporary file paths.
- If you read a file that exists but has empty contents you will receive a system reminder warning in place of file contents.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__dismiss_task
tools.description:
Withdraw a background-task chip you previously created with spawn_task.

Call this when a suggestion you flagged is now stale, superseded, or irrelevant — e.g. you (or the user) already fixed it in this session, or you spawned a better-scoped replacement. To replace a chip: call spawn_task with the new suggestion first, then dismiss the old task_id.

Only chips the user hasn't acted on can be withdrawn from the queue. If the user already started or dismissed the task, the result says so (a dismissed task's copy kept for later is withdrawn too) — do not retry.

tools.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

Flag an out-of-scope issue for a separate background task.

Call this when you notice something worth fixing that would bloat the current change — dead code, stale docs, missing coverage, a confirmed TODO, or a security issue spotted in passing. Don't flag vague code-smell observations, trivial fixes you can do inline, or low-confidence hunches. A chip appears for the user; one click spins it off into its own session. tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

13	/// Writes a change set. **Must not open its own transaction** — the caller
14	/// owns it, because the rows and the cursor advance have to commit together.
15	public protocol HealthSampleWriting: Sendable {
16	    func apply(_ changeSet: HealthChangeSet, in db: Database) throws -> HealthApplyCounts
17	}
18	
19	/// Persists samples for one `HealthDomain`. This slice wires up `.bodyMass`
20	/// only; the table and this type are domain-agnostic, but no other domain is
21	/// enabled, tested, or claimed to work.
22	public struct HealthSampleStore: HealthSampleWriting, TimelineProviding, @unchecked Sendable {
23	    public let domain: String
24	    public let healthDomain: HealthDomain
25	    public let sourceSystem: String
26	    private let db: Database
27	    private let clock: any Clock
28	    private let zone: ZoneContext
29	
30	    public init(db: Database, healthDomain: HealthDomain = .bodyMass,
31	                sourceSystem: String = "healthkit",
32	                clock: any Clock = SystemClock(),
33	                zone: ZoneContext = ZoneContext(TimeZone.current)) {
34	        self.db = db
35	        self.healthDomain = healthDomain
36	        self.sourceSystem = sourceSystem
37	        self.domain = healthDomain.rawValue
38	        self.clock = clock
39	        self.zone = zone
40	    }
41	
42	    private var nowText: String { ISO8601DateFormatter().string(from: clock.now) }
43	    private func iso(_ date: Date) -> String { ISO8601DateFormatter().string(from: date) }
44	
45	    @discardableResult
46	    public func apply(_ changeSet: HealthChangeSet, in db: Database) throws -> HealthApplyCounts {
47	        var inserted = 0, updated = 0, deleted = 0
48	
49	        for sample in changeSet.added where sample.domain == healthDomain {
50	            let existing = try db.query("""
51	                SELECT id FROM health_sample WHERE source_system = ? AND external_id = ?;
52	                """, [.text(sourceSystem), .text(sample.externalID)]).first?.string("id")
53	            // Identity is (source_system, external_id): the same string from a
54	            // different source is a different sample, never an update of this one.
55	            try db.run("""
56	            INSERT INTO health_sample
57	                (id, source_system, external_id, domain, start_at, end_at, value, unit,
58	                 source_name, recorded_at, recorded_tz_offset_minutes, deleted_at)
59	            VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, NULL)
60	            ON CONFLICT(source_system, external_id) DO UPDATE SET
61	                start_at    = excluded.start_at,
62	                end_at      = excluded.end_at,
63	                value       = excluded.value,
64	                unit        = excluded.unit,
65	                source_name = excluded.source_name,
66	                recorded_at = excluded.recorded_at,
67	                deleted_at  = NULL;
68	            """, [
69	                .text(existing ?? UUID().uuidString), .text(sourceSystem),
70	                .text(sample.externalID), .text(sample.domain.rawValue),
71	                .text(iso(sample.start)), .text(iso(sample.end)),
72	                sample.value.map { SQLValue.real($0) } ?? .null,
73	                sample.unit.map { SQLValue.text($0) } ?? .null,
74	                sample.sourceName.map { SQLValue.text($0) } ?? .null,
75	                .text(nowText),
76	                zone.offsetMinutes.map { SQLValue.integer(Int64($0)) } ?? .null
77	            ])
78	            if existing == nil { inserted += 1 } else { updated += 1 }
79	        }
80	
81	        // Soft delete. A source withdrawing a sample is a fact about the
82	        // source, not permission to erase what was already recorded.
83	        for externalID in changeSet.deletedExternalIDs {
84	            deleted += try db.run("""
85	                UPDATE health_sample SET deleted_at = ?
86	                WHERE source_system = ? AND external_id = ? AND deleted_at IS NULL;
87	                """, [.text(nowText), .text(sourceSystem), .text(externalID)])
88	        }
89	
90	        return HealthApplyCounts(inserted: inserted, updated: updated, deleted: deleted)
91	    }

93	    public func liveSampleCount() throws -> Int {
94	        Int(try db.query("""
95	            SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM health_sample
96	            WHERE source_system = ? AND domain = ? AND deleted_at IS NULL;
97	            """, [.text(sourceSystem), .text(healthDomain.rawValue)])
98	            .first?.int("n") ?? 0)
99	    }

101	    public func isDeleted(externalID: String) throws -> Bool {
102	        guard let row = try db.query("""
103	            SELECT deleted_at FROM health_sample WHERE source_system = ? AND external_id = ?;
104	            """, [.text(sourceSystem), .text(externalID)]).first else { return false }
105	        return !row.isNull("deleted_at")
106	    }

108	    public func entries(from: String, to: String) throws -> [TimelineEntry] {
109	        guard let range = DateRange(from: from, to: to) else { return [] }
110	        // Normalised to UTC before it reaches SQL. `start_at` is stored as a
111	        // UTC `...Z` string, so comparing it lexically against a caller's
112	        // `+03:00` text would be wrong by three hours — and silently so.
113	        let bounds = range.utcTextBounds
114	        return try db.query("""
115	        SELECT id, external_id, start_at, value, unit, source_name
116	        FROM health_sample
117	        WHERE source_system = ? AND domain = ? AND deleted_at IS NULL
118	          AND start_at >= ? AND start_at < ?
119	        ORDER BY start_at;
120	        """, [.text(sourceSystem), .text(healthDomain.rawValue),
121	              .text(bounds.start), .text(bounds.end)])
122	        .compactMap { row in
123	            // Samples always carry a full instant, so their span is a point and
124	            // the fit is always `.definite`. Computed through the same API as
125	            // Laboratory so the two domains cannot drift apart on what a range
126	            // means.
127	            guard let id = row.string("id"), let start = row.string("start_at"),
128	                  let occurrence = PartialDateTime(storedText: start, precision: .instant,
129	                                                   zone: .unknown),
130	                  let fit = occurrence.fit(in: range) else { return nil }
131	            let value: ValuePresentation
132	            if let v = row.double("value") {
133	                value = .quantity(text: String(v), unit: row.string("unit"))
134	            } else {
135	                value = .missing(reason: LabMissingReason.notReportedBySource.rawValue)
136	            }
137	            return TimelineEntry(
138	                domain: domain, kind: "sample", recordTable: "health_sample", recordID: id,
139	                occurrence: occurrence, basis: .occurrence,
140	                title: healthDomain.rawValue, detail: row.string("source_name"),
141	                value: value, lifecycle: nil, rangeFit: fit)
142	        }
143	    }

3	public struct SyncOutcome: Sendable, Hashable {
4	    public let counts: HealthApplyCounts
5	    public let advancedTo: [UInt8]?
6	}

8	/// One incremental sync, with the property that matters: **the imported rows
9	/// and the cursor advance commit together.**
10	///
11	/// The read from the provider happens outside the transaction; only the write
12	/// is inside it. If the write throws, the transaction rolls back and the anchor
13	/// keeps its previous value, so the next run re-reads the same range. An anchor
14	/// that advanced past rows that were never persisted would skip them for good.
15	public struct HealthSyncService: Sendable {
16	    private let db: Database
17	    private let provider: any HealthProvider
18	    private let anchors: SyncAnchorStore
19	    private let writer: any HealthSampleWriting
20	    private let healthDomain: HealthDomain
21	    private let anchorKey: String
22	
23	    public init(db: Database, provider: any HealthProvider, writer: any HealthSampleWriting,
24	                healthDomain: HealthDomain = .bodyMass, clock: any Clock = SystemClock(),
25	                anchorKey: String? = nil) {
26	        self.db = db
27	        self.provider = provider
28	        self.writer = writer
29	        self.healthDomain = healthDomain
30	        self.anchors = SyncAnchorStore(db: db, clock: clock)
31	        self.anchorKey = anchorKey ?? healthDomain.rawValue
32	    }
33	
34	    public func currentAnchor() throws -> [UInt8]? {
35	        try anchors.load(anchorKey)?.token
36	    }
37	
38	    @discardableResult
39	    public func syncOnce() async throws -> SyncOutcome {
40	        let previous = try anchors.load(anchorKey)?.token
41	        let changeSet = try await provider.changes(in: healthDomain, since: previous)
42	        do {
43	            return try db.transaction {
44	                let counts = try writer.apply(changeSet, in: db)
45	                try anchors.save(domain: anchorKey, token: changeSet.nextAnchor)
46	                return SyncOutcome(counts: counts, advancedTo: changeSet.nextAnchor)
47	            }
48	        } catch {
49	            // The rows and the advance both rolled back. Record why, without
50	            // clearing the last good anchor.
51	            try? anchors.recordFailure(domain: anchorKey, message: String(describing: error))
52	            throw error
53	        }
54	    }
55	}

551	    /// that changed only the specimen or the collection date previously did

553	    /// `lab_observation_metadata_revision` with the actor, the reason and the
554	    /// list of fields touched.
555	    @discardableResult
556	    private func updateObservationMetadataImpl(
557	        id observationID: String, _ edit: LabObservationMetadataEdit, withinTransaction: Bool = false
558	    ) throws -> LabMetadataOutcome {
559	        guard let existing = try db.query("""
560	            SELECT id, report_id, catalog_analyte_id, match_origin, match_confidence,
561	                   specimen_kind, specimen_text, collected_at, collected_precision,
562	                   collected_tz_offset_minutes, collected_tz_id
563	            FROM lab_observation WHERE id = ?;
564	            """, [.text(observationID)]).first else {
565	            throw LabError.observationNotFound(observationID)
566	        }
567	        guard edit.touchesAnything else { return .unchanged(observationID: observationID) }
568	
569	        let oldReportID = existing.string("report_id")
570	        let oldAnalyteID = existing.string("catalog_analyte_id")
571	        let oldSpecimenKind = existing.string("specimen_kind")
572	            .flatMap(SpecimenKind.init(rawValue:)) ?? .unknown
573	        let oldSpecimenText = existing.string("specimen_text")
574	        let oldCollectedAt = PartialDateTime(
575	            storedText: existing.string("collected_at") ?? "",
576	            precision: TimePrecision(rawValue: existing.string("collected_precision") ?? "")
577	                ?? .unknown,
578	            zone: ZoneContext(
579	                offsetMinutes: existing.int("collected_tz_offset_minutes").map(Int.init),
580	                identifier: existing.string("collected_tz_id"))) ?? .unknown
581	
582	        let newReportID = edit.reportID.resolve(oldReportID)
583	        let newAnalyteID = edit.catalogAnalyteID.resolve(oldAnalyteID)
584	        let newSpecimenKind = edit.specimenKind.resolve(oldSpecimenKind, cleared: .unknown)
585	        let newSpecimenText = edit.specimenText.resolve(oldSpecimenText)
586	        let newCollectedAt = edit.collectedAt.resolve(oldCollectedAt, cleared: .unknown)
587	
588	        var changed: [String] = []
589	        if newReportID != oldReportID { changed.append("report_id") }
590	        if newAnalyteID != oldAnalyteID { changed.append("catalog_analyte_id") }
591	        if newSpecimenKind != oldSpecimenKind { changed.append("specimen_kind") }
592	        if newSpecimenText != oldSpecimenText { changed.append("specimen_text") }
593	        if newCollectedAt != oldCollectedAt { changed.append("collected_at") }
594	        guard !changed.isEmpty else { return .unchanged(observationID: observationID) }
595	
596	        let operation = { () throws -> LabMetadataOutcome in
597	            let number = Int(try db.query("""
598	                SELECT COALESCE(MAX(revision_number), 0) AS n
599	                FROM lab_observation_metadata_revision WHERE observation_id = ?;
600	                """, [.text(observationID)]).first?.int("n") ?? 0) + 1
601	            let revisionID = UUID().uuidString
602	            try db.run("""
603	            INSERT INTO lab_observation_metadata_revision
604	                (id, observation_id, revision_number, report_id, catalog_analyte_id,
605	                 match_origin, match_confidence, specimen_kind, specimen_text,
606	                 collected_at, collected_precision, collected_tz_offset_minutes,
607	                 collected_tz_id, changed_fields, actor, reason_text, recorded_at)
608	            VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?);
609	            """, [
610	                .text(revisionID), .text(observationID), .integer(Int64(number)),
611	                oldReportID.map { SQLValue.text($0) } ?? .null,
612	                oldAnalyteID.map { SQLValue.text($0) } ?? .null,
613	                existing.string("match_origin").map { SQLValue.text($0) } ?? .null,
614	                existing.string("match_confidence").map { SQLValue.text($0) } ?? .null,
615	                .text(oldSpecimenKind.rawValue),
616	                oldSpecimenText.map { SQLValue.text($0) } ?? .null,
617	                oldCollectedAt.isKnown ? .text(oldCollectedAt.text) : .null,
618	                .text(oldCollectedAt.precision.rawValue),
619	                oldCollectedAt.zone.offsetMinutes.map { SQLValue.integer(Int64($0)) } ?? .null,
620	                oldCollectedAt.zone.identifier.map { SQLValue.text($0) } ?? .null,
621	                .text(changed.joined(separator: ",")), .text(edit.actor),
622	                edit.reasonText.map { SQLValue.text($0) } ?? .null, .text(nowText)
623	            ])
624	            try db.run("""
625	            UPDATE lab_observation SET
626	                report_id                   = ?,
627	                catalog_analyte_id          = ?,
628	                match_origin                = ?,
629	                match_confidence            = ?,
630	                specimen_kind               = ?,
631	                specimen_text               = ?,
632	                collected_at                = ?,
633	                collected_precision         = ?,
634	                collected_tz_offset_minutes = ?,
635	                collected_tz_id             = ?
636	            WHERE id = ?;
637	            """, [
638	                newReportID.map { SQLValue.text($0) } ?? .null,
639	                newAnalyteID.map { SQLValue.text($0) } ?? .null,
640	                // A mapping a person set is attributed to the person, and a
641	                // cleared mapping carries no origin at all.
642	                edit.catalogAnalyteID.isChange
643	                    ? (newAnalyteID == nil ? .null : .text("user"))
644	                    : (existing.string("match_origin").map { SQLValue.text($0) } ?? .null),
645	                edit.catalogAnalyteID.isChange
646	                    ? (newAnalyteID == nil ? .null : .text("user_assigned"))
647	                    : (existing.string("match_confidence").map { SQLValue.text($0) } ?? .null),
648	                .text(newSpecimenKind.rawValue),
649	                newSpecimenText.map { SQLValue.text($0) } ?? .null,
650	                newCollectedAt.isKnown ? .text(newCollectedAt.text) : .null,
651	                .text(newCollectedAt.precision.rawValue),
652	                newCollectedAt.zone.offsetMinutes.map { SQLValue.integer(Int64($0)) } ?? .null,
653	                newCollectedAt.zone.identifier.map { SQLValue.text($0) } ?? .null,
654	                .text(observationID)
655	            ])
656	            return .updated(observationID: observationID, revisionID: revisionID,
657	                            revisionNumber: number, changedFields: changed)
658	        }
659	        return try withinTransaction ? operation() : db.transaction(operation)
660	    }

706	                observation.matchOrigin = match.origin

711	                // showing an unexplained gap.

713	                observation.matchConfidence = candidates.map(\.analyteID).joined(separator: " ")

717	        }

I have thoroughly explored `Sources/AlmanacCore`. Here is the full report.

## 1. Overall module/directory layout (`Sources/AlmanacCore`)

| Path | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `Backup/BackupService.swift`, `Backup/SHA256File.swift` | Skeleton SQLite-online-backup snapshotting + a SHA256 hashing helper. `restore()` is deliberately unimplemented. |
| `Documents/DocumentStore.swift` | Content-addressed file storage (`FileSystemDocumentStore`) + metadata/link rows (`LabDocumentStore`); backup does not yet cover these files. |
| `Health/HealthProvider.swift` | `HealthProvider` protocol seam for HealthKit (Linux can't import HealthKit), `HealthDomain` enum, `FakeHealthProvider` test double. |
| `Health/HealthSampleStore.swift` | Persists `health_sample` rows for one domain (`.bodyMass` is the only wired-up domain); upsert + soft-delete + `TimelineProviding` conformance. |
| `Health/HealthSyncService.swift` | One incremental sync cycle: read outside transaction, write+anchor-advance inside one transaction. |
| `Laboratory/*.swift` (9 files) | The largest module — lab report/observation revisioning, conflict detection via `SourceOrdering`, catalog matching, unit compatibility, text folding. |
| `Nutrition/*.swift` | `NutritionCatalog` (read-only query seam over reference tables), `NutritionReferenceImporter` (ATTACHes and copies a bundle built by `tools/nutrition`), `NutritionBasis`, `GeneralAtwater` (energy estimation). |
| `Persistence/*.swift` | `Database` (thin SQLite wrapper), `Migration.swift`/`MigrationRunner.swift`, and 10 numbered migration files (schema history), `SQLiteError.swift`. |
| `Provenance/*.swift` | `LicenceGroup`, `NutrientQualifier`, `SourceIdentifier` — cross-cutting provenance/licensing types shared by Nutrition (and referenced by Laboratory). |
| `Sync/SyncAnchorStore.swift` | Generic, domain-keyed opaque-token sync-anchor persistence (HealthKit-anchor-shaped) with failure recording that never clears the last good anchor. |
| `Time/*.swift` | `Clock`/`SystemClock`/`FixedClock`, `PartialDateTime`/`PartialDateTimeSpan` (coarse date model), `TimeModel` (logical-day/DST-aware boundary math). |
| `Timeline/*.swift` | `Timeline` (merges per-module `TimelineProviding` entries into one sorted feed), `TimelineEntry`. |

No `Hydration` directory exists at all today.

## 2. Query/data-access layer — caching/indexing

- There is no repository/ORM abstraction beyond `Database` (`Sources/AlmanacCore/Persistence/Database.swift`) — a thin wrapper (`query`, `run`, `execute`, `transaction`) directly over the C SQLite API. Each module (`LabStore`, `HealthSampleStore`, `NutritionCatalog`, `SyncAnchorStore`, `LabDocumentStore`) is a plain struct holding a `Database` and writing raw SQL inline.
- **No caching exists anywhere** — no result cache, no memoization, no statement cache (every `query`/`run` calls `sqlite3_prepare_v2` fresh; `SQLiteError`/no `sqlite3_prepare_v3` persistent-cache flag). `grep -rn "cache\|Cache"` returns zero hits in `Sources/AlmanacCore`.
- **Indexing exists but only ad hoc**, one `CREATE INDEX` per migration as each feature needed it: e.g. `idx_lab_observation_time`, `idx_lab_revision_current`, `idx_health_sample_domain_time` (Migrations002_004), `idx_nutrition_food_name_fold` (008), `idx_nutrition_log_time`/`idx_nutrition_log_food` (009), `idx_nutrition_portion_lookup` (010), `idx_backup_manifest_created_at`. There's no index-review/EXPLAIN tooling and no query planner instrumentation. `Database.userVersion` is the only introspection surface.
- `LabStore.entries(from:to:)` explicitly notes range-filtering is done in Swift over an unfiltered SQL pull "because the placing time is chosen per row... Pushing it into SQL is a later optimisation, not a correctness change" — a flagged future performance TODO in the code itself (`Sources/AlmanacCore/Laboratory/LabStore.swift:936-938`).

## 3. Hydration logging — does anything exist?

**No.** Searched all of `Sources` and `Tests` for "hydration" case-insensitively: the only hit is a code comment in `Tests/AlmanacCoreTests/GeneralAtwaterTests.swift:52` about *chemical* hydration uplift in Atwater factors — unrelated to water/drink logging. There is no `HydrationLoggingService`, no `hydration_log` table/migration, no hydration domain in `HealthDomain` (which only has `sleep, workouts, activeEnergy, restingEnergy, steps, heartRate, hrv, bodyMass`). This is a from-scratch build.

The closest analogous pattern to build from is `Migration009` (`nutrition_log` table) + the (missing) store that should sit on top of it — see §6 below, that's also a gap.

## 4. Offline/sync/conflict-resolution — reusable pattern

Yes, there is a strong, generalizable pattern, split into two layers:

**a) Generic incremental-sync anchor persistence** — `Sources/AlmanacCore/Sync/SyncAnchorStore.swift`:
```swift
public struct SyncAnchor: Sendable, Hashable {
    public let domain: String; public let token: [UInt8]?
    public let lastSynced: Date?; public let lastError: String?
}
public struct SyncAnchorStore {
    public func load(_ domain: String) throws -> SyncAnchor?
    public func save(domain: String, token: [UInt8]?) throws
    public func recordFailure(domain: String, message: String) throws
}
```
Domain-keyed, opaque-blob token (works for any provider's cursor, not just HealthKit), and `recordFailure` never clears the last-good anchor — so a failed sync retries the same range rather than skipping or restarting. This is directly reusable as the "sync recovery" building block for a hydration offline queue.

**b) Atomic write+anchor-advance pattern** — `HealthSyncService.syncOnce()` (`Sources/AlmanacCore/Health/HealthSyncService.swift`): reads from the provider *outside* a transaction, but writes the rows and advances the anchor together *inside* one `db.transaction { }`. If the write throws, the anchor keeps its old value so nothing is skipped. This is the template for any "offline queue drains, applies, then commits its own cursor" flow.

**c) Conflict resolution (source-ordering based)** — Laboratory's `SourceOrdering`/`LabStore.upsertReport` (`Sources/AlmanacCore/Laboratory/LabSourceOrdering.swift`, `LabStore.swift:143-360`, from commit `9928137 fix: preserve laboratory revisions, conflicts and source ordering`). Key ideas that generalize well to hydration/offline-queue conflicts:
- `SourceOrdering` (`.unavailable` / `.sequence(Int)` / `.issuedAt(String)`) with a `compare(to:)` that returns `nil` (unrankable) rather than guessing — arrival order is never treated as authority.
- `LabReportOutcome` enum encodes every outcome explicitly: `.created`, `.unchanged`, `.updated`, `.replayIgnored` (a resend of an old version), `.staleIgnored` (a source-ranked-older version), `.conflict` (unrankable — held for human resolution via `needsHumanResolution`).
- `UnrankedImportPolicy` (`.applyAndFlag` vs `.holdAsConflict`) — an injected policy, not a hardcoded choice, for what to do when arrival order can't be trusted.
- `resolveReportConflict(id:accept:actor:reason:)` — explicit human-in-the-loop resolution, atomic with applying/discarding the conflicting version, and requires non-empty `actor`/`reason` (audit trail).
- Fingerprinting (`reportFingerprint`, SHA256-based) to detect "identical content resent" vs "a genuinely new version" vs "a replay of a version already seen in history" — this is exactly the shape needed to dedupe an offline queue that retries after a dropped network call.

This is the pattern to reuse/generalize for a hydration offline queue + sync recovery, rather than reinventing one.

## 5. HealthKit integration — existing stubs, what's missing

Existing (Linux-safe, platform-free):
- `HealthProvider` protocol (`Sources/AlmanacCore/Health/HealthProvider.swift`) — `requestAuthorisation(for:)`, `changes(in:since:) -> HealthChangeSet`. Explicit doc comment: *"The concrete `HealthKitProvider` belongs in the iOS target and is the only place `import HealthKit` may appear."*
- `HealthDomain` enum: `sleep, workouts, activeEnergy, restingEnergy, steps, heartRate, hrv, bodyMass` — names are Almanac's own, HK type-mapping is explicitly deferred ("per the spec's HealthKit map, which is not available here and must not be guessed").
- `FakeHealthProvider` — in-memory test double, used by `Tests/AlmanacCoreTests/HealthSyncTests.swift`.
- `HealthSampleStore` — persistence + timeline provider, but **only `.bodyMass` is wired up, tested, or claimed to work** (explicit comment at `HealthSampleStore.swift:19-21`); the table is domain-agnostic but every other domain (including anything hydration-relevant like `.dietaryWater`, which doesn't even exist in the enum) is unimplemented.
- `HealthSyncService` — generic sync-once orchestration (works for any domain via `HealthSampleWriting`).

**Missing / TODO for the two planned efforts:**
- No `import HealthKit` anywhere in the repo (expected — it can't compile on Linux) and correspondingly **no iOS target exists yet** to host `HealthKitProvider`.
- No `.dietaryWater` (or equivalent) case in `HealthDomain` — needed for hydration write-back to HealthKit.
- No write path to HealthKit at all — `HealthProvider` is read-only (`changes(in:since:)`); logging hydration and pushing it *to* HealthKit needs a new protocol method or a separate writer seam.
- No local-notifications code anywhere (`grep -i "notification"` — zero hits in Sources/Tests).

## 6. "Nutrition API" — Swift-side integration point

- `tools/nutrition/almanac_nutrition` is a **separate Python package** (CLI/importer/QA tooling: `bundle.py`, `dictionary.py`, `sources/{usda,ciqual,cofid,afcd}.py`, etc.) that builds a SQLite "bundle" file — it is a build-time pipeline, not a runtime API.
- **Package.swift has no separate Nutrition target/product** — Nutrition is just a subfolder (`Sources/AlmanacCore/Nutrition/`) inside the single `AlmanacCore` target.
- The Swift-side integration point is `NutritionReferenceImporter.importBundle(at:)` (`Sources/AlmanacCore/Nutrition/NutritionReferenceImporter.swift`) — it `ATTACH DATABASE`s the Python-built bundle file and copies verified rows into `nutrition_food`, `nutrition_value`, `nutrition_nutrient`, `nutrition_source`, `nutrition_food_name` in one transaction, with licence/qualifier verification re-checked in Swift (`BundleGuard.assertShippable`, `verifyLicenceGroups`, `verifyQualifiers`) rather than trusted blindly from the bundle.
- Read access at runtime is `NutritionCatalog` (`food(_:)`, `values(for:basis:)`, `bases(for:)`, `energy(for:basis:)`, `search(_:limit:)`).
- There is a `nutrition_log` table (Migration009 — food-eaten logging: grams, quantity, `eaten_at`/precision/timezone, soft-delete, one revision table) but **no corresponding Swift store/service exists for it** — only the migration. This is a genuine gap (parallel to the missing hydration store) and is the closest existing schema pattern for how a `HydrationLoggingService`-backed table should probably look (source_system/external_id identity for dedup, `*_at`/`*_precision`/`*_tz_offset_minutes`/`*_tz_id` columns, soft `deleted_at`, single revision table since it's a small/simple fact).

## 7. Date/time handling (for DST/leap-year/timezone test planning)

- `Clock` protocol (`Sources/AlmanacCore/Time/Clock.swift`) — `SystemClock` and a thread-safe `FixedClock` (settable/advanceable) injected everywhere instead of `Date()` calls, so time can be pinned deterministically in tests.
- `TimePrecision` enum (`unknown, year, month, day, hour, minute, instant`) with rank ordering — nothing below the source's stated precision is ever invented.
- `ZoneContext` (`Sources/AlmanacCore/Time/PartialDateTime.swift`) — optional `offsetMinutes` + optional `identifier`; both nullable because historical records often state neither, and an unknown zone is a recorded fact, never silently defaulted to device-local.
- `PartialDateTime` — coarse/partial timestamp stored as an **unpadded ISO-8601 prefix string** (`"2019"`, `"2019-03"`, `"2019-03-14"`, `"2019-03-14T08:10"`, full instant), chosen so lexical string sort == chronological sort. Regex-validated per precision including a real calendar-rollover check (rejects Feb 30) via `Calendar(identifier: .gregorian)`.
- `PartialDateTimeSpan.swift` defines `DateRange` (used by `LabStore`/`HealthSampleStore` for range queries) with `utcTextBounds` — explicit UTC normalization before SQL text comparison, called out in `HealthSampleStore.entries` as important because `start_at` is stored as UTC `...Z` text and comparing it lexically against a caller's `+03:00` text would silently be wrong by hours.
- `TimeModel` (`Sources/AlmanacCore/Time/TimeModel.swift`) — the DST-aware core: maps instants to `LogicalDay` via `Calendar` with explicit `TimeZone`, supports `.midnight` or `.wakeOffset(hours:)` day boundaries, and computes day bounds by **adding one calendar day, not 86,400 seconds**, specifically so a DST spring-forward day is 23h and fall-back is 25h.
- **DST/timezone tests already exist** in `Tests/AlmanacCoreTests/TimeModelTests.swift`: `testDSTSpringForwardDayIsShorterThan24Hours`/`testDSTFallBackDayIsLongerThan24Hours` (Europe/London, BST transitions), `testEveryDayOfAYearRoundTrips` (365-day full-year round-trip using Riyadh/wakeOffset), `testRiyadhMidnightBoundary`, `testWakeOffsetPullsSmallHoursIntoPreviousDay`. This is a solid template to extend for leap-year (`2028-02-29`, `2100` non-leap-century edge) and additional timezone edge cases (half-hour offsets like `Asia/Kolkata`, Southern-hemisphere DST, historical zone-rule changes) — none of those specific edge cases are covered yet.

## 8. Package.swift — targets, products, platforms

```swift
// swift-tools-version:5.9
platforms: [.iOS(.v17), .macOS(.v14)]
products: [.library(name: "AlmanacCore", targets: ["AlmanacCore"])]
targets: [
    .target(name: "CSQLite", path: "Sources/CSQLite", sources: ["sqlite3.c"], publicHeadersPath: "include", cSettings: [...FTS5, JSON1, DQS=0, foreign_keys=1, THREADSAFE=1, OMIT_DEPRECATED]),
    .target(name: "AlmanacCore", dependencies: ["CSQLite"], path: "Sources/AlmanacCore"),
    .testTarget(name: "AlmanacCoreTests", dependencies: ["AlmanacCore"], path: "Tests/AlmanacCoreTests")
]
```
- Only 3 targets total: `CSQLite` (vendored SQLite C amalgamation, vendored specifically "so the Linux core and the iOS app compile against a byte-identical SQLite" — comment already anticipates an iOS app), `AlmanacCore` (the platform-free library), `AlmanacCoreTests`.
- **No app/executable target exists.** `platforms: [.iOS(.v17), .macOS(.v14)]` sets minimum deployment for the *library*, which is necessary but not sufficient for an app.
- Feasibility note for effort #2: SwiftPM **can** declare an iOS-app-shaped target only as a `.target`/`.executableTarget` that gets embedded in an actual Xcode app wrapper, or via `.executableTarget` on macOS for a command-line tool — SwiftPM alone cannot produce a signed, installable `.app` bundle/Info.plist/asset catalog for iOS (no `iOSApplication` product type in SwiftPM as of tools-version 5.9). In practice this means: add a new SwiftUI-source `.target` (e.g. `AlmanacApp` or similar) to `Package.swift` depending on `AlmanacCore`, containing the views/services, but pairing it with an actual Xcode project/workspace (or Tuist/XcodeGen-generated `.xcodeproj`) that wraps that target as the iOS app product, handles entitlements (HealthKit, notifications), Info.plist, and code signing — none of which SwiftPM manages natively. This should be flagged explicitly in the plan as a repo-structure decision (Package.swift target + separate Xcode project vs. full migration to an Xcode workspace).
